{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent, and no option is preferred.

THE QUESTION: a check RUN can end in a qualified state, mostly passing, with a named part either blocked or changed on purpose. qs, 2026-09-04: "An acceptance run that proved everything qs is responsible for but could not exercise one plan (blocked by the simulator) had to be either `passing` or `blocked`." dev_storyflow, 2026-09-25: "My walk ended 31/35: the 4 'failures' were the intended tightening, which a parity check proved. `passing` overstates that and `failing` misreports it." Verification.status is the only outcome any rollup reads, so today the qualification lives in `findings`, where no computation and no list view looks (measured: fact:root-cause-a-run-has-one-status-and-its-qualification-reaches-no-rollup-2026-09-28).

THE OPTIONS, in the reporters' words where they gave them:

(a) A NEW STATUS. qs: "a `partial` status". dev_storyflow: "passing, with 4 expected-change assertions". Cheapest to write. ⚠️ It owes every reader a ruling: does it satisfy `verified`, clear the unproven-capability gap, count in coverage_report? That was the qs record's own warning.

(b) STRUCTURED RUN COUNTS beside an unchanged status, for example assertions total, passing, expected_change and blocked on the run. The status keeps its meaning, and every rollup can print "31/35, 4 expected" beside it. No reader's answer changes. It costs properties on Verification and a rendering change in loop_status.

(c) PER-CLAUSE RESULTS. qs: "per-clause findings so a check can pass for the part under the project's control and be blocked elsewhere". The most precise option, the nearest to dec:idea-a-finding-carries-its-bounds's structured results, and the most expensive.

(d) SPLIT THE RUN. The changed or blocked part becomes its own Verification on the same target, and the tightening's ChangeEvent retires it with INVALIDATES plus a note, a shape the same reporter praised four times in the same report. No schema change. The cost is more nodes per walk and a split the author must make by hand.

(e) READ SIDE ONLY. Keep the schema and show `findings` (or its first line) wherever a status is listed. The cheapest option, but the qualification still reaches no computation.

🛑 THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: four "failures" that are the intended change are STALE EXPECTATIONS. The check as written is failing. The discipline the design already has is to update the check with the change and re-run it to 35/35, and a qualified-pass vocabulary could become the easy way to wave failures through. qs's blocked case does not carry this objection, which suggests the two shapes may not want one answer.
